models.name: Waka
models.description: The beautiful Waka, with some great looking planks, cork rails and a twin FCS fin set up. It's freshly polished and in our showrrom. Holding true to a traditional fish shape inspired by its founder Steve Lis, the Waka combines speed with a classic ride. Skatey, loose, and lively, it loves racing down the line or carving around softer surf that would be a struggle on most shortboards. The Waka is a shop favorite for the same reason the fish shape has never gone out of style—it’s so darn fun! The design of the Waka focuses planing capability and speed generation in a small package. A wider outline makes up for lack of length, allowing this fish to be ridden shorter than most other shapes.The…

models.name: Tern
models.description: The beautiful Tern, built in our original CedarRail construction is in the showroom and is ready to wax! This board was built/shaped at Eddie Vedder's Ohana Fest in California so it's got rhythm in it's bones, some beautiful cedar planks and functional two plus one fin set up. The Tern is a pintail mid-length that draws influence from retro shapes to bring style and flow to waves with a little more juice. Born from wanting to push some of our classic mid-length boards like the Seed and Sapling into bigger and steeper surf, the Tern excels with control at speed. The Tern features a sleek, pulled in outline with a very drawn out pintail for holding tight in the pocket. It has a good amount…

models.name: The Cutwater
models.description: Finished Board Specs 9’6" x 22 7/8″x 3 1/8″ / Volume 77.39 L For 'Tailored Dims', we'll reach out with a form to tell us what you're thinking about. Designed purely for tip-time, the Cutwater is our take on the classic noserider for those under-chest-high log sessions. Our rocker is inspired by old-school shapers that flipped foam blanks around, nose-to-tail, to get maximum tail-kick and a low nose. A deep, natural, concave under its beak runs to a flat-bottom midsection and a super-swept square-tail. Dimensions like those, along with 50/50 rails, are why this board allows you to get a walk in while you ride. So, either lock yourself in the pocket or drag along for a slow dance on the tip.

models.name: The Dreadnought
models.description: This big gun was built for one thing: exhilarating survival. Designed with a fistful of new internal construction details that make it formidable and fast, it has a mostly flat bottom and slight V in the full-shaped pintail. Its weighted construction fearless before monster waves, this big gun runs chatter-free ahead of bone-crushing curls.

models.name: The Drifter
models.description: Finished Board Specs 12' x 24" x 3 1/2" For 'Tailored Dims', we'll reach out with a form to tell us what you're thinking about. The 12′ Drifter was designed with long gentle stomach-high peelers in mind. The 12-0 originated from our popular 10’ Waterlog template. It’s been refined for long, slow beach-break, where the first of these boards appears regularly to steal waves from way outside where the stand-ups roam. The Drifter turns best from the tail, sinking and pivoting around the fin, but walk forward and it trims right out and picks up amazing speed even as its consistent belly makes rolling into turns surprisingly easy. This board is enjoyed most by bigger surfers who are looking for…

This “pig” surfboard type carries its less-than-flattering name in honor of its outline. A heritage board that looks unusual today, it was at one time found on every beach in California. The “pig” needed some new justice, and for subtlety of design, there was no better input to be found than that of pig-master Gene Cooper of Cooperfish Surfboards. models.description: Finished Board Specs 10’6" x 23 3/4″x 3 1/16″ / Volume 90.78 L For 'Tailored Dims', we'll reach out with a form to tell us what you're thinking about. A classic retro that will never go out of style, this pintail noserider is a true beauty. Despite its length, the sweeping pintail and pinched 50/50 rails make this board seem almost slight next to the logs we ride in small surf. A gentle belly through most of the board’s length combined with ultra-fine rails make this board responsive and lively. Great in head-high surf, boards of this style are also ridden at breaks like Sunset.

models.name: The Pandan
models.description: Finished Board Specs 6'-11-3/4"x 20-1/8″x 2-3/16″ / Volume 39.96 For 'Tailored Dims', we'll reach out with a form to tell us what you're thinking about. The Pandan was originally conceived as a pro-level funshape designed with the help of seven-time world champ Layne Beachley. Looking for something for her home break, we worked up a slender funshape up to fit her advanced skills. Besides the graceful single-to-double concaves and tight little squash tail. we designed it as a low-rocker board with a flat entry and hotted it up with a curvy, spooned-out step deck forward. This board has the full outline fun-shape surfers want, but with performance elements pros look for.

models.name: The Radicle

Named after the first rootlet to emerge from a germinating seed, we think of the Radicle as a next-gen surfboard. Its design sprouts from a blend of pro free-surfer Dave Rastovich’s style and our continuing quest to evolve wood board construction methods. The flat V in the tail gives excellent high-speed response, quick to slice big, deep lines across the faces of hollow dredgers like those at Pipeline and Backdoor. A double to single concave from tail to nose channels water past the fin, allowing the board to react quicker and carve on a dime.

Stretching out the fish outline, the Shearwater inhabits a sweet spot among shapes we really love. Paddle it with the ease of a midlength and feel the acceleration of the tail end of a fish. Bending wood to the super-deep double concaves that run between fins canted at almost twenty degrees, we managed a version of perhaps the most radical bottom ever put under a surfboard. Operating on principles literally extracted from aeronautics, boards of this type represent possibly the most extreme design innovation to be applied to surfboards since the fin. brands.short_description: Gold Coast custom performance, mid-length, and fish designs from shaper Stuart D'Arcy.

models.name: A-Bomb
models.description: It's all about volume with shortboard performance... Made to make the most out of dismal surf conditions, you can catch more waves while maintaining performance. The a-bomb is ridden 4 to 6 inches shorter and 1 to 2 inches wider than your normal dimensions. It’s crazy how versatile the super fast and fun a-bomb design is. Put a smile on your dial.. Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate D'Arcy Surfboards ~ 5'5 A-Bomb ~ "I contacted Darc towards the end of last Winter to get a summer board shaped up. I wanted something to be more of a step down to my regular performance shortboard (5'9 Pit Pro). Considering the waves on offer in South Aus are small during summer. I needed a board to be…

models.name: Cutaway Fish
models.description: The Cutaway Fish is a reboot of the Superfish with some performance-enhanced changes. Pulling in the outline between the feet and behind the back foot, allows the board to turn faster in a tighter arc, whilst still maintaining speed and smooth control without losing any paddle power. Smooth Operator Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: Disco Twin
models.description: As surfing got more radical in the 80‘s with 360’s, airs, rounder roundhouses and more vertical re-entries, design experimentation went wild! Shorter, curvier and more outline, the flyer swallow twin perfected and performance tested by the likes of Mark Richards and Martin Potter inspired the disco twin. Fast and loose. Goes really fast in fluro! rip, tear, lacerate... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: Dragon
models.description: The dragon is an all round short board. A little more out line and volume in the foil allows the bigger surfer to maintain speed without losing performance. Fast and reliable in most conditions, this is my all round weapon of choice. Fire it up... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: Frequent Flyer
models.description: The link between the Bomb and the performance short board. The Frequent Flyer is ridden 2 to 3 inches shorter and a little wider in the nose and tail than your normal short-board. Made to perform best in slower or choppy waves, really fast in super clean waves and like the name suggests, quick off the mark. If you want to add some speed and spark to your day to day surfing the Frequent Flyer is it! speed defies gravity... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: Grom
models.description: Grom The Grom shape comes into play when the young surfer takes control of his equipment. Shaped to suit a performance level and wave type is critical at this stage of development. Customise is wise. Tested and proven around the world by Junior Champions. Smash it up... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate - Beginner

models.name: Gun
models.description: The D’Arcy Gun and Tow Series is the result of hardcore testing by the D’Arcy Team in some of the heaviest waves in Australia, Indonesia and Hawaii. Combined with the strongest materials and best workmanship money can buy, these boards will come through for you when you need them most. In the water! Trust in experience... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: Mid-length Magic
models.description: The Mid-length Magic is a mid-length shape usually between 6'8 - 7'6 forced into riding a bigger board through injury.I made a flat rocker (easy paddle) super hull (easy turn) 7'2 x 21'1/2" x 2'5/8 round tail single . inspired by the Wayne Lynch evolution model. It not only got me back in the water but also had me frothing on the free feeling. The connection to the power of the wave and the easy control in all size waves is amazing. I've been working on different fin systems twins, twinzers with channels. I first call it my Mid Length Crisis but after some customers call it their magic board I renamed it The Mid Length Magic. So fast and effortless to paddle. *All board prices based on…

models.name: Mini Long
models.description: Like the name suggests the mini long is the little brother to the long. Inspired by the transition from longboard to shortboard made popular by Bob McTavish and Wayne Lynch, their soul, style and grace in the water depict new shapes and this is the evolution of the mini long made to be graceful in all conditions. style and grace... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate - Beginner

models.name: Pirate Door
models.description: This model came about from living in the U.S in 2013, riding mainly slow, sloppy waves. It's a super fun mini board and what it lacks in length it makes up in outline. A wide nose and tail with a semi-hull entry through to single double barrel concave with vee kick out the tail. With a flatter rocker, takeoff is easy and speed is not a problem. The concave to vee bottom lets it flow from one rail to another so you can put the pedal to the metal and go vertical into and beyond the lip. The volume of the Superfish, the grace of the Waterbird and the release of the Abomb Made to plunder... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate - Beginner

models.name: Pit Pro
models.description: Designed for the contest ready surfer to max their heat points, it's fast and loose with plenty of drive for the aerial attack. A sweet bottom curve and clean outline combined allows performance surfing at it's best. For the pro in the pit... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: Single Slave
models.description: 70s shortboard revolution! Speed and radical maneuvers in small to medium waves shorter, wider, thinner, looser and way more curve will still maintain the single fin style of surfing. If you just want to add some grace to your surfing or you remember the lines of days gone by, a change is as good as a holiday. speed blur Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: Sleepwalker Long
models.description: Not your traditional long board design...working in the 90‘s with Michel Demont (World Champion Longboarder) on his contest demands and his free surfing at home in tahiti, we came up with an all rounder. A combination of classic smooth lines and modern curve designs, a little more curve in the bottom combined with a smooth outline makes an ideal shape for today’s progressive surfing style. smooth soul... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate - Beginner

models.name: Snub
models.description: Developed for Pottz in the 90’s for the pro tour... A lower nose entry and more nose area makes catching waves and keeping up speed in slow soft waves easy. Using a standard short board tail kick and outline, the snub performs like your favourite short board in small gutless waves. Get air if you dare... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: Step Up
models.description: The ultimate island hopping back-up As the standard boards are getting smaller, I've designed a board to perform in the 4-8 foot bracket Bigger than your shortboard and smaller than a gun, this is an essential for your board bag for those tropic adventures Stand tall...

models.name: Superfish
models.description: A super short twin with a wide nose and tail design that gives the feel of a longer board when on its rail . More volume to catch more waves, a rolled vee up front and flat vee through the keels and curve to suit .The keel fins allow it to glide through turns .A double barrel vee in the tail helps it release when necessary. soul to glide Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: The Slingshot
models.description: The Slingshot was made to compliment the pit pro and all its contest savvy attributes, allowing the surfer who surfs very junky waves all the time, the chance to open up the speed between turns whilst maintaining flow. get high and fly... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate

models.name: Ugly Betty
models.description: Volume, volume, volume... The Ugly Betty I built for myself in the UK to maximise paddle volume and keep a performance feel in powerless waves.Combining chimed rails and flat to concave deck line, the Ugly Betty paddles fast . Having a vee barrel concave bottom maintains speed through turns. A full nose outline allows you to ride it shorter so it easer to manoeuvre in small waves ... Designed for surfers who like an easy paddle and a fast and smooth ride. Great for all waves up to 4 feet... Fun in the Sun... Suitable Skill Level Pro - Intermediate - Beginner

models.name: Waterbird
models.description: Working with team rider Jimmy McMillan towards a shape to fuse the performance shortboard with the speed and flow of the Superfish model which Jimmy loved cruising on after getting back into the water from a serious spinal injury. Enter the Waterbird! Capitalising on volume and outline for maximum wave catchability, fast and stable because of its width yet highly manoeuvrable because of its curves and fin configuration. Quad fins equal less drag and your best fun will be in small to medium waves. For those cruisy surfers who like to lay a line down, set the rail and glide through the turn. Birds are all about freedom and this board really gets you there. ...swoop, carve, float, fly!…

brands.name: Wayne Lynch Surfboards
brands.short_description: Victorian surf craft from Australian surfing legend Wayne Lynch, including the Evo, Hybrid, Performance, and Unison longboard.

models.name: Evo
models.description: The Evo Design is a refinement of one of the very first boards I did back in 1968 whilst working in John Arnold’s Surf Shop in South Australia where I first began seriously shaping. When I was very young, there was a board called a Teardrop. One of my friends had one. That board had a specific design. It had a very wide tail combined with a tapering plan-shape right to the nose which was pointy and if you had grabbed it by the nose, held it up, it looked like a drop of water. At the time I was riding early balsa wood, thick railed, heavy longboard that had nothing refined about it. Whenever I swapped boards with my friend, I was amazed by how free it was and how different it felt to my…

models.name: Hybrid
models.description: 6’10 x 20 3/4 x 2 7/8 Hybrid thruster The Hybrid. A concept that has been derived by blending specific elements of my two favourite boards, the ‘Performance’ and the ‘Evo’. Aesthetically pleasing softer curves through the plan shape, not to pointy-not to round, combined with the lower entry rocker of the Evo and the bottom shape of the Performance, the Hybrid is to date, the most versatile board in my quiver. Suited to a variety of different waves, from your average mushy beach break to long peeling point break walls and steep hollow reef breaks. FCS Fusion thruster setup Sage deck fade spray- blue pinline - golden yellow bottom Satin finish Fins not Included

models.name: Performance
models.description: With around 40 years of research and design, the Performance board is my absolute go to board for the best, hollowest and most powerful waves, in which, I’ve spent majority of my time surfing down south on the rugged Victorian coastline. Built for waves of consequence, I’ve surfed these boards in Indonesia, Hawaii, and Fiji as part of the development process. The design is really quite simplistic. The bottom shape being single to double concave to double concave Vee to Vee off the tail, all very subtle as to me it’s all about blend. As the boards get longer and for larger waves, I reduce the surface area in the back quarter, increasing the Vee through the tail taking away to double concave…

models.name: Single Fin
models.description: The Single Fin. Reno Abellira had shaped a few boards for the Lorne surf shop when he was in Vic for the 1977 bells contest. I walked into the shop some time after and saw the 6’11 swallowtail sitting in the racks and immediately bought it. The Reno was one of my all time favourite boards, but had some aspects I wanted to adjust, especially the nose rocker as it was just a bit too flat. Furthering that, I’ve refined and changed that board over many years by increasing the entry rocker, adding a modern bottom and rails whilst trying to maintain the original plan shape. Typically, surfboards are an ever developing process. I’ve always described shaping as part art, part craft and part…

models.name: Unison Longboard
models.description: The Unison Longboard I’ve been asked many times over the years if I’ll ever make a mal. After spending most of my life trying to get off them, I’ve realised now that’s it’s quite a fun and interesting thing for me to do, revisiting that way of surfing again. This design is a modern refined take on the involvement era mal’s we used to ride in the mid sixties. Blended concave through the nose leading to subtle roll though the tail, wide point back, 50/50 rails. It’s responsive off the tail, maintains speed when in trim and really stable on the nose creating a simultaneous flow between the rider, the board and the wave. I’ve really enjoyed creating this board, and now on the small days, I’m…
